message.reasoning:
I need to examine the key escape and unescape methods, which are package-private static methods, meaning my test class needs to live in the org.jsoup.nodes package to access them directly.

I'm planning to write EntitiesTest there, importing Entities and Document.OutputSettings, plus using Charset encoders to test non-ASCII branches. I'm mapping out test cases covering entity lookups for characters like ampersand, angle brackets, quotes, and copyright symbols across the different escape modes.

I'll also use an ASCII-only encoder to force the numeric escape fallback for characters like Lstrok that aren't in the base entity map but are encodable only outside ASCII, and verify extended-mode entities like Amacr get properly matched. I should add edge cases too, like an empty string input and the overloaded escape method using default OutputSettings.

I'm wary of guessing Document.OutputSettings' default behavior (charset, default escapeMode) since I don't have its source in front of me, so I need to be careful not to assume unverified defaults when writing this test.

Actually a safer test is to verify that escape(string, out) equals escape(string, out.encoder(), out.escapeMode()), which checks delegation without guessing default behavior. For unescape(String), I'm thinking through the branch where the input string doesn't contain "&" at all.

For strings with "&", I'm tracing the regex matching for entities like 😀 or &, checking whether the numeric group parses as hex or decimal, and noticing a suspicious condition `charval != -1 || charval > 0xFFFF` -- that "||" looks wrong since it should likely be checking both bounds with "&&". This looks like the actual injected defect I need my test suite to catch.

I realize the condition should likely use && instead of ||, meaning the ">0xFFFF" check never actually filters anything since the first part is already true whenever charval isn't -1. So out-of-range values like astral plane codepoints (e.g. an emoji at 0x1F600) would get truncated by the char cast instead of being rejected, which is exactly the boundary case I should test for.

So (char)128512 narrows to 62976, a private-use-area character, which I can assert deterministically since it's traced directly from the code rather than guessed. I should also test named entity lookup cases: "&" resolving to "&", and an unknown entity like "&foobar;" remaining unchanged since it's not in the entity map.

Looking closer, unescape only checks the full map, never the base map directly—but since fullArray is a superset containing all base entries too, that's still correct behavior. I'll also test numeric unescaping, like hex "?" converting to '?'.

I should also check malformed numeric cases, like decimal mode containing hex digits ("&#1F;"), which would throw a NumberFormatException during parsing and fall back to treating the match as a literal string. And I need to verify entities without a trailing semicolon, like "&amp" without ';', since the regex marks the semicolon as optional.

I'll cover multiple entities in one string, strings with no "&" returning unchanged, empty string input, strings with "&" but no valid match, and proper handling of trailing text after the last match via appendTail. I also want to confirm the escape() method works correctly on empty input despite capacity calculations, and test extended ASCII characters.

For encoder-based fallback, I'll use "Ā" (0x100) which exists in the full map but not the base map—with an ASCII encoder that can't handle 0x100, this should fall back to the numeric form "Ā", while extended mode should produce "Ā". I also want to verify a character like '<' present in both maps correctly resolves to "<", and I'll construct an actual US-ASCII encoder to force the numeric fallback path for unmapped non-ASCII characters, plus test the straightforward canEncode-true branch for plain ASCII.

Now I'm tracing through the regex group numbering for unescaping—group1 captures the full entity content (either the name or the #-prefixed numeric form), group2 captures the optional hex indicator, and group3 captures the numeric digits, with named entities leaving groups 2 and 3 null.

I also need to place the test class in the same package, org.jsoup.nodes, so it can access the package-private Entities methods without extra imports.

I'm assuming Document.OutputSettings has its standard jsoup defaults—UTF-8 charset and base escape mode—since that's typical jsoup behavior, and my tests focus on verifying delegation consistency rather than hardcoding exact default values. Now I'll draft the full test file, including coverage for the EscapeMode enum's base mode.

Planning out specific test methods: verifying enum values and valueOf lookups for base/extended, checking empty string escaping, confirming known characters like "<" map correctly in base mode, and testing extended-only characters like Amacr that should escape differently depending on whether the encoder can handle them directly or falls back to numeric entities.

For the remaining cases, I need tests for encodable ASCII characters that pass through unchanged, non-encodable characters outside any entity map that should fall back to numeric escapes (like a snowman character), mixed strings combining multiple escaping categories, delegation through output settings, and unescape behavior when there's no ampersand present at all.

Then I'm covering unescape scenarios: named entities with and without trailing semicolons, unknown named entities left untouched, decimal and hex numeric references in both cases, and a malformed numeric reference where a hex digit appears in what should be a decimal escape, causing the parse to fail and the literal text to remain unchanged.

I'm also noting the out-of-range numeric case where a codepoint above the char range gets truncated, deliberately documenting this as a known defect, plus a test combining multiple entities and plain text together.

Remaining cases cover empty string input returning empty output, a lone "&" with no match left unchanged, and entities sitting right at the start or end of a string. I'm also checking case-sensitivity in named entity lookup -- "&" resolves since it's in the full map, but "&Amp;" stays unescaped since the map keys are case-specific. Now I'll move to writing the final test code with these assertions.

For a specific extended entity like Amacr, I'm confirming its character code and noting that the map check for named entities takes priority over encoder capability, so escaping that character produces "Ā" regardless of encoder. In base mode, since that entity isn't in the base map, the same character with an ASCII encoder should fall back to a numeric escape instead.

Now I need a character that's neither ASCII-encodable nor present in either entity map, so I'm trying to verify whether something like the snowman symbol is absent from the full entity list before settling on a safe test character.

I'll instead use a Private Use Area code point like U+E000, since it's guaranteed to have no named entity and will reliably fall back to a numeric reference like "" for the ASCII encoder test. Then for the output settings escaping test, I'm setting up a simple string with angle brackets, ampersands, and quotes to verify proper escaping behavior.

For the encoder itself, I need a non-null encoder object -- I'll use US-ASCII's encoder for cases testing the numeral fallback branch, and UTF-8's encoder for cases testing the canEncode-true branch, since UTF-8 can encode nearly any valid character and will pass unmapped characters through literally rather than escaping them numerically.

Now I'm drafting the test class with the needed imports and verifying that escape/unescape are package-private static methods callable directly from a same-package test. I also want to double check the char overflow math for the surrogate boundary case where codepoint 128512 wraps around as a 16-bit char value.

So the condition evaluates true, confirming the truncated char is produced — this gives me a solid fault-detecting test asserting unescape("😀") equals "\uF600", documenting the defect where || should be && for range checking. I should also add a boundary test at exactly 0xFFFF (65535) to confirm correct behavior at the edge, separate from the defect case.

I'm also considering testing 65536, where the truncation bug produces a null character instead of the expected value, and I'll keep the test using a decimal entity rather than hex for simplicity. I should verify the zero case too, where charval=0 takes the same branch and correctly produces a null character as expected behavior.

Another good case is testing a number that overflows Integer range, like 99999999999, which should trigger a NumberFormatException and leave the literal unchanged since charval stays at -1. I'll also verify unescape works correctly on strings with multiple entities and surrounding text, including when an entity appears at the very end with no trailing text, and check that escape() returns an empty string for empty input.

For completeness, I'll add a test confirming that escape(string, outputSettings) properly delegates to escape(string, encoder, escapeMode) by comparing results from both calls using a real Document.OutputSettings instance, since that class should work standalone without needing a full Document setup.
